claims.text: High-temperature X-ray diffraction can be used to study high-temperature oxidation behaviour in materials.
High-temperature X-ray diffraction can be used to study phase stability in materials.
The proposed method is applicable to various high-temperature materials.
Exposure to high-temperature conditions can affect crystal structure and phase composition.
In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction permits monitoring of structural changes during high-temperature oxidation.
Monitoring crystal structure and phase composition in situ will improve understanding of high-temperature oxidation behaviour and phase stability.
There is a current lack of understanding of high-temperature oxidation behaviour and phase stability.
Conditions above 500°C are an example of the relevant high-temperature regime.
The effectiveness of high-temperature X-ray diffraction depends on the specific material and experimental conditions.
Failure to observe significant changes in crystal structure and phase composition during oxidation would falsify the proposed method's utility.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule treats absence of structural or phase changes as failure, even though observing no change can itself be evidence of phase stability and therefore a valid result of the proposed method.
